assessment.title: Intermediate DSA Diagnostic Assessment
assessment.description: 35 multiple-choice questions across seven DSA topics. Baseline indicator of conceptual and problem-solving knowledge.

questions.text: What is the time complexity of accessing the element at index i in an array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Array indexing uses pointer arithmetic on the base address, so any index is reached in constant time.

questions.text: After `arr = [1,2,3]; for i in range(len(arr)): arr[i] = arr[i] * 2`, what is arr?
questions.explanation: Each element is doubled in place; no new elements are appended.

questions.text: Applying the in-place 'remove duplicates from sorted array' algorithm to `[0,0,1,1,1,2,2,3,3,4]` yields a resulting length of:
questions.explanation: The unique values are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — five in total.

questions.text: Using Kadane's algorithm on `[-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4]`, the maximum subarray sum is:
questions.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has sum 6, which is the maximum.

questions.text: An array of n integers has every element appearing twice except one appearing once. The array cannot be modified. The minimum extra space to find the unique element is:
options: O(n) using a hash set is required
questions.explanation: XOR of all elements cancels the paired duplicates, leaving the unique element in O(1) space.

questions.text: In a 0-indexed string, `"abc"[1]` evaluates to:
questions.explanation: 0-indexed strings start at 0, so index 1 is the second character.

questions.text: What relationship holds between the strings "listen" and "silent"?
options: They are anagrams of each other
They share the same prefix of length 4
questions.explanation: Both strings contain the same characters with the same frequencies, i.e. they are anagrams.

questions.text: In Python, `"hello"[::-1]` returns:
questions.explanation: A slice with step -1 reverses the string.

questions.text: Ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters, is "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" a palindrome?
questions.explanation: After filtering and lowercasing, it reads 'amanaplanacanalpanama', which is symmetric.

questions.text: The minimum time complexity to decide whether two strings of length n are anagrams, using a character-count array:
questions.explanation: One pass to build the count and one pass to verify give O(n); the alphabet is constant.

questions.text: Binary search requires that its input array is:
questions.explanation: Binary search repeatedly discards a half based on a comparison that is only valid on sorted data.

questions.text: The worst-case time complexity of insertion sort on n elements is:
questions.explanation: Insertion sort performs up to ~n^2/2 comparisons on a reversed input.

questions.text: In a sorted array of 1,000,000 elements, roughly how many comparisons does binary search require in the worst case?
questions.explanation: log2(1,000,000) is approximately 20, so the loop runs about 20 times.

questions.text: Which sorting algorithm is stable and has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: Merge sort is stable and is O(n log n) in all cases; heapsort is not stable and quicksort is O(n^2) in the worst case.

questions.text: Which input triggers quicksort's O(n^2) worst case when the pivot is chosen as the first element?
options: An array of distinct random elements
questions.explanation: Choosing the first element of an already-sorted array produces maximally unbalanced partitions at every level.

questions.text: Accessing the k-th element of a singly linked list of n nodes, with only a head pointer, takes:
options: O(k), i.e. O(n) in the worst case
questions.explanation: Linked lists do not support random access; you must traverse from the head.

questions.text: Which of these operations is NOT O(1) in a singly linked list when only the head pointer is available?
options: Retrieving the value of the head
questions.explanation: Reaching the last node requires traversal of all n nodes.

questions.text: Which technique detects a cycle in a singly linked list using O(1) extra space?
questions.explanation: Floyd's two-pointer technique detects a cycle in O(n) time and O(1) space.

questions.text: Applying the standard iterative three-pointer reversal to `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> NULL` produces:
questions.explanation: The iterative reversal reverses the next-pointer chain, producing the reverse order.

questions.text: Finding the middle node by (a) counting the nodes then traversing to n/2, versus (b) slow and fast pointers. The asymptotic complexities are:
questions.explanation: Both visit each node a constant number of times: counting is one full pass plus a half pass; slow/fast is a single pass with two pointers.

questions.text: A recursive function must have:
options: A return statement of type int
questions.explanation: Without a base case, the recursion does not terminate.

questions.text: With f(0)=0, f(1)=1, and f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2) for n>=2, what is f(4)?
The time complexity of the naive recursive Fibonacci implementation is:
questions.explanation: Each call branches into two subcalls, giving roughly phi^n growth.

questions.text: For f(n)=n*f(n-1) with f(0)=1, what is f(3)?
In a language with proper tail-call optimisation, the maximum stack depth of a tail-recursive factorial(n) is:
questions.explanation: TCO converts the tail call into a jump, so no new stack frame is allocated per recursive call.

questions.text: An in-order traversal of a binary search tree visits its keys in:
questions.explanation: By the BST property, left subtree keys are smaller and right subtree keys are larger.

questions.text: The maximum number of nodes at level L of a binary tree (root at level 0) is:
questions.explanation: Each node at level L-1 has two children, so the maximum grows as 2^L.

questions.text: A binary tree has 15 nodes. Its minimum possible height (root at level 0) is:
questions.explanation: A complete tree with 2^0 + 2^1 + 2^2 + 2^3 = 15 nodes has height 3.

questions.text: Which traversal visits a node after both of its children, and is the correct order for freeing all nodes?
questions.explanation: Post-order visits children before the parent, so children can be freed while the parent is still reachable.

questions.text: The time complexity of finding the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a general (non-BST) binary tree of n nodes is:
questions.explanation: Without the BST ordering property, both subtrees may need to be explored, giving a worst case of O(n).

questions.text: Which two properties are needed for a problem to be a good fit for dynamic programming?
questions.explanation: DP exploits optimal substructure by caching solutions to overlapping subproblems.

questions.text: The naive recursive Fibonacci is exponential. With top-down memoisation, its time complexity becomes:
questions.explanation: Each of the n subproblems is computed once and reused, so the total time is O(n).

questions.text: With coin denominations [1, 5, 6, 9], the minimum number of coins needed to make 11 is:
questions.explanation: The optimal combination is 5+6, using 2 coins. The greedy choice (9+1+1) uses 3.

questions.text: For the 0/1 knapsack with items (w=2,v=3), (w=3,v=4), (w=4,v=5), (w=5,v=8) and capacity 7, the maximum value is:
questions.explanation: The best combination is (w=2,v=3) + (w=5,v=8), total weight 7 and value 11.

questions.text: The length of the longest common subsequence of "ABCBDAB" and "BDCABA" is:
questions.explanation: "BCBA" and "BDAB" are both common subsequences of length 4, and no length-5 common subsequence exists.
